permutationLabel: Age 71, short history, rapid weight loss — pseudoachalasia (cardia cancer)
summary: 71-year-old man with 4 months of dysphagia to solids and liquids, regurgitation and 10 kg weight loss. Short history + age + weight loss = pseudoachalasia from a cardia cancer until proven otherwise.

inputs.hpi: Four months of food and fluids sticking at the lower end of the chest, with regurgitation of undigested food. Lost 10 kg. Ex-smoker. No previous reflux symptoms.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected pseudoachalasia — cardia carcinoma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Achalasia-type dysphagia with a 4-month history and 10 kg weight loss aged 71 — pseudoachalasia from a cardia carcinoma until proven otherwise. Urgent OGD with retroflexed views and CT.

emergencyLevel.note: Red flag, not an emergency: urgent (2-week) outpatient endoscopy. CLAUDE.md: red flags warrant expedited outpatient review, not ER redirect.

guideline.name: European guidelines on achalasia — UEG and ESNM recommendations
guideline.section: Pseudoachalasia: suspect with older age, short symptom duration and marked weight loss; endoscopy (with retroflexion) and cross-sectional imaging/EUS before achalasia treatment
guideline.citation: Oude Nijhuis RAB, Zaninotto G, Roman S, et al. United European Gastroenterol J. 2020;8:13–33.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (oesophageal and stomach cancer)
guideline.section: Dysphagia (any age) or age ≥55 with weight loss: urgent OGD
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (last updated 2023).

rationale: Elderly permutation: same achalasia pattern, but age, short history and heavy weight loss make malignant pseudoachalasia the must-not-miss diagnosis.
